summary: Discovery call to understand Tidewater Labs' model selection needs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Key constraints: 1) multilingual support (EN/ES/FR/JA), 2) long context for multi-doc workflows (~64k tokens target), 3) function/tool calling for retrieval and custom tools, 4) strict data residency and SOC2 requirements. Discussed candidate open models (Llama 2, Mistral, Falcon, MPT), tradeoffs (context length vs latency/cost), and Redwood options for Dedicated GPU pools or Private VPC deployment. Agreed next steps to run benchmarks and share pricing/security docs.
topics: Open model comparison: Llama 2 vs Mistral vs Falcon vs MPT
Tool/function calling support and retrieval integration
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Security/compliance: SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (CTO - Tidewater), Ethan Park (ML Lead), Liam O'Neill (Infra)
Shared: security packet (link: https://redwood.ai/security.pdf), benchmark template (link: internal)

[00:00] Sofia Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood. Marco and I will run through model selection and deployment options. Priya, Ethan, Liam — could you quickly share goals for today's call?
[00:18] Priya Desai: Sure, thanks. High level — we're evaluating how to power our multi-doc assistant across legal and research workflows. Need multilingual support, long context window, and ability to call our retrieval tools/functions. Also strong security — SOC2 and customer data residency.
[00:35] Ethan Park: To add, we expect 60k to 80k token contexts for some workflows — mainly concatenated docs + metadata. Latency target is <1s per token for interactive but we're flexible if batching helps. Cost is a big factor, we prefer open models if performance is acceptable.
[00:52] Marco Alvarez: Got it. So three axes: context length, multilingual quality, and tool-calling. Plus deployment: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Quick clarification: when you say 60k–80k tokens, is that worst-case or common?
[01:05] Ethan Park: Worst-case; median is around 10–15k. But we need the system to handle the tails without failure.
[01:12] Liam O'Neill: Also, compliance side — we need control plane in our VPC for the pilot, and KMS integration for keys. Probably Private deployment for sensitive clients, but we'll evaluate Dedicated for broader rollout.
[01:24] Sofia Chen: Makes sense. High level, open models that teams usually evaluate now are Llama 2 variants (2-70B historically), Mistral 7B/Chat, Falcon, and MPT. Each has tradeoffs: some support long context extensions natively, others rely on chunking + retrieval. Redwood can host these models on Hosted, Dedicated reserved pools, or in Private VPC.
[01:45] Marco Alvarez: On the runtime side, our serving supports KV cache & prefix caching to handle long sequences efficiently. For contexts >32k we typically evaluate specialized long-context variants or use sliding window + retrieval to avoid full attention on the entire context. Performance/latency will vary by model and quantization profile.
[02:05] Priya Desai: Do you have verified benchmarks for multilingual? Spanish and French are must-haves, Japanese is a nice-to-have. Some vendor benchmarks are... optimistic.
[02:16] Sofia Chen: We do Redwood-verified profiles — we'll share the multilingual perf table. Quick note: Llama family tends to be strong across many languages with larger parameter sizes; Mistral shows good zero-shot in European languages; Falcon has mixed results for Asian languages. We'll send model-specific examples.
[02:32] Ethan Park: Tool calling — we need function calling for our retrieval microservice, plus ability to call custom tools (sanitizer, redactor). Any limitations?
[02:42] Marco Alvarez: Our API supports streaming plus structured function/tool calling. For Private deployments, you can run the same interface with local tool endpoints. We have examples of function-call schema and a pattern for safe redaction before returning results. Sometimes transcription of function names is noisy in ASR but that's separate.
[03:00] Liam O'Neill: On Private — what does network topology look like? We need ready-to-run packages for air-gapped clients and a control plane that can live in our VPC.
[03:09] Sofia Chen: Private offers a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package. We support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs streamed to your SIEM, and KMS/HSM integrations. I'll pass the security whitepaper.
[03:22] Marco Alvarez: Back on models — for a 64k token target, options are: 1) Use a model variant built for long context (few variants exist), 2) Use segmented retrieval and KV cache to approximate longer context, or 3) Combine retrieval + on-the-fly summarization. Each impacts latency and cost differently. We recommend running a perf run with your workload to quantify.
[03:45] Ethan Park: If we go Dedicated, can we pin specific model weights and quantization? We want stable latency across peak traffic.
[03:53] Marco Alvarez: Yes, Dedicated lets you pin model versions and quantization profiles. We can also reserve GPU types (A100/H100 equivalence depending on region). Autoscaling policies can be tuned for burst vs steady.
[04:07] Priya Desai: Cost math — we have to compare token costs + infra. Is Redwood able to provide recommendations on quantization and batching to hit our cost targets?
[04:16] Sofia Chen: That's Redwood Optimize. We run workload analysis and recommend batching sizes, KV cache settings, and quantization profiles to balance cost and latency. We'll include recommended profiles for the models you're interested in.
[04:28] Ethan Park: Any concerns about hallucination when doing tool-calls/retrieval? We need verifiable citations.
[04:35] Marco Alvarez: Retrieval + tool calling pattern helps — enforce deterministic tool outputs, verify with confidence thresholds, and use reranking/evidence-first prompts. We also support structured output and output validators in the runtime.
[04:48] Priya Desai: For multilingual, will we need separate model per language or a single multilingual model?
[04:55] Marco Alvarez: If you need top-tier quality in Japanese, sometimes a dedicated East-Asia-tuned model is better. For European languages, larger multi-lingual models often suffice. We recommend running a small eval set in each language. We'll provide eval harness templates.
[05:10] Liam O'Neill: Security checklist — SOC2, ISO? Data residency?
[05:15] Sofia Chen: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO certifications for Hosted, and Private deployments can be configured to meet data residency requirements. We'll share the compliance pack and the SSO/KMS integrations doc.
[05:26] Ethan Park: There's also concern about inference caching and PII. Can Redwood scrub cached prefixes or control retention?
[05:32] Marco Alvarez: Yes, retention policies are configurable per tenant. We can disable prefix caching or configure TTLs. For Private, you control the storage.
[05:40] Priya Desai: Timeline — we'd like a pilot in Q1. Assuming benchmarks look good, pilot on Dedicated for a subset of customers and Private for high-security accounts.
[05:50] Sofia Chen: Sounds reasonable. Recommendation: run a 1-week benchmark with your worst-case traces and a median workload. Marco can help set that up.
[05:58] Marco Alvarez: I'll send the benchmark template and ask for sample prompts and language mix. For models to test, propose: Llama 2 70B (quantized), Mistral mix, Falcon x/xl, and MPT-30B. We'll include long-context strategies per model.
[06:14] Ethan Park: Curious — any Redwood-verified long-context models yet?
[06:18] Sofia Chen: We have early profiles for long-context variants; they're experimental but promising. For production, we often combine retrieval + KV cache. We'll mark the long-context variants as experimental in the report.
[06:28] Liam O'Neill: Regarding Private deployment cost — is there a minimum commitment?
[06:33] Sofia Chen: Private pricing involves a platform fee + support tier; Dedicated has reserved capacity commits. I'll include ballpark numbers in the pricing doc.
[06:42] Priya Desai: Great. Let's recap and owners.
[06:46] Sofia Chen: Recap quick: 1) Redwood to share pricing and security pack (Sofia) — due 2027-01-03. 2) Marco to send benchmark template + model list — due 2027-01-03. 3) Tidewater to provide sample traces + language mix (Ethan) — due 2027-01-06. 4) Schedule SE deep dive week of 2027-01-10 (Sofia + Priya).
[07:06] Ethan Park: Sounds good. One small Q — function calling latency: do you have numbers when calling an internal retrieval service over VPC?
[07:13] Marco Alvarez: Latency depends on network and thread pool sizing. In Dedicated we can colocate retrieval to reduce RTT; expect an additional 10–50ms per call if nearby. We'll include best practices in the benchmark doc.
[07:25] Priya Desai: Thank you. Any concerns on our side?
[07:27] Sofia Chen: No major blockers. We'll get the artifacts over and align on pilot scope.
[07:35] Liam O'Neill: I'll follow up with security contact for SSO and KMS integration details.
[07:39] Sofia Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:42] Priya Desai: Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: Some transcription artifacts around product names (Mistral vs Mistral-LM), occasional speaker mislabels, and punctuation issues.
